findings.text: Move the palace out of the repo to $HOME/.mempalace/palace and default PALACE_PATH there
findings.motivation: The palace currently lives inside the working tree at ./data/mempalace, which is an artifact of how the Docker deployment bind-mounts it rather than a deliberate choice. That couples 555MB of irreplaceable user data to a checkout: it is duplicated per clone, it sits under a host/VM shared mount (which already produced two concurrent writers against one ChromaDB SQLite file), and any repo-level cleanup or re-clone endangers it. $HOME/.mempalace/palace is MemPalace's own default and the conventional home for user data.
findings.behavior: docker-compose.yml:7 bind-mounts ./data/mempalace into the container, and Makefile:12 defaults PALACE_PATH to $(CURDIR)/data/mempalace, so the launchd unit exports MEMPALACE_PALACE_PATH pointing back into the repo. MemPalace's own default location is never used, and the repo-local path is load-bearing for both deployment modes.
findings.approach: Relocate the store to $HOME/.mempalace/palace, flip the Makefile PALACE_PATH default, and repoint or drop the docker-compose volume so both supervisors agree. Add a one-shot migration step that stops every writer first and refuses to proceed if the destination is already a non-empty palace, so the move cannot silently merge or clobber two stores. Keep PALACE_PATH overridable for anyone who wants the old layout.
findings.success_signal: mempalace_status reports palace_path under $HOME/.mempalace/palace with the full drawer count intact, and a fresh clone of the repo contains no palace data.
